3231182.background: Idaho has a near-total abortion ban since 2022. Idahoans United for Women and Families gathered signatures to put a constitutional-style initiative restoring abortion access up to viability on the November 2026 ballot. Idaho votes roughly 60-65% Republican; initiatives need a simple majority. Similar measures passed in Kansas, Ohio, Missouri, Montana.

actors.public: Sponsor; won signature qualification and litigated ballot titles; argues doctors are leaving and the ban endangers women. Moderate funding, likely supported by national reproductive-rights groups.
actors.private: Knows Idaho is the hardest terrain yet; aims to win independents and Republican women on medical-emergency framing; a close loss would still be framed as progress.

actors.name: Idaho Republican establishment (Legislature, AG Raul Labrador)
actors.public: Strongly anti-abortion; challenged ballot language and initiative process; legislators have tried to tighten signature and ballot rules.
actors.private: Would use procedural or legal tools to blunt or delay the measure; wants a decisive defeat to deter future initiatives.

actors.name: Anti-abortion coalition (Right to Life of Idaho, churches)
actors.public: Campaigning for No; strong church networks especially among LDS and evangelical voters.
actors.private: Will frame the measure as extreme and 'abortion up to birth'; relies on high Republican turnout.

actors.name: Idaho electorate
actors.public: Heavily Republican but with libertarian streak; voters passed Medicaid expansion by initiative in 2018 (61%).
actors.private: Some Republicans quietly support exceptions; turnout composition in a midterm decides it.

events.name: Court ruling removing or altering the measure's ballot language
